77999.subject: Cosmos Labs Tells All EVM Chains to Halt
77999.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Cosmos Labs](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/cosmos-labs-urges-evm-chains-halt-shared-bug-drains-three-networks)**[ tells every chain on its EVM module to halt and patch](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/cosmos-labs-urges-evm-chains-halt-shared-bug-drains-three-networks)

* **[Coinbase](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/coinbase-launches-tokenized-stocks-on-base)**[ puts four US tech stocks onchain on Base](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/coinbase-launches-tokenized-stocks-on-base)

* **[A thin Pendle pool](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pendle-oracle-move-liquidates-usd36-million)**[ triggers $36 million of Morpho liquidations](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pendle-oracle-move-liquidates-usd36-million)

* **[Bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-stalls-a-cent-below-usd80-000-as-altcoins-give-back-weekend-gains)**[ stalls one cent below $80,000](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-stalls-a-cent-below-usd80-000-as-altcoins-give-back-weekend-gains)

* **[LayerZero](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/layerzero-unveils-atlas-exchange-engine)**[ ships an exchange engine that burns 75% of fees into ZRO](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/layerzero-unveils-atlas-exchange-engine)

Cosmos Labs told every public chain running its EVM module below v0.6.2 or v0.7.2 to halt on Tuesday morning. Three chains that run it — MANTRA, TAC and KiiChain — had already been drained between Aug. 20 and Aug. 22, and two of them are still frozen.

KiiChain has put the only numbers on the damage. An attacker took 148 million KII, worth roughly $9.7 million, [repeating the same technique 18 times against different targets](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/cosmos-labs-urges-evm-chains-halt-shared-bug-drains-three-networks) before the chain halted. Cosmos Labs has published no security advisory. The v0.6.2 and v0.7.2 release notes carry boilerplate about "important security fixes" with no CVE, no advisory reference, and nothing identifying a live exploit path.

KiiChain says the upstream fix is partial: only the underflow has been patched, and two of the three defects that had to line up remain open. The XRPL EVM sidechain still pins a fork of v0.6.1, below the floor Cosmos Labs named, and was producing blocks normally on Tuesday afternoon.

**Read more below!**

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### BLOCKCHAINS

## Cosmos Labs Urges EVM Chains To Halt

Cosmos Labs [recommended on Tuesday](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/cosmos-labs-urges-evm-chains-halt-shared-bug-drains-three-networks) that any public blockchain running a Cosmos EVM module below v0.6.2 or v0.7.2 "immediately halt the blockchain and upgrade." The recommendation reaches an unknown number of networks sharing one open-source codebase. Caption: 

# The bond market has something to say again

Economist Chris Sims [describes](https://www.imes.boj.or.jp/en/conference/2008/Session6.pdf) the Fed’s monetary policy actions in the 1970s as “stepping on a rake.” Three times, the Fed aggressively raised interest rates to fight inflation. Three times, inflation was temporarily subdued, only to come back stronger.

Sims attributed this to a feedback loop of higher interest rates causing higher deficits causing higher interest rates — a loop that can only be broken when investors believe the government has the will to balance its budget. Otherwise, rate hikes become counterproductively inflationary.

“Economic theory makes clear that in an environment of uncertainty about future fiscal policy, monetary policy instruments may lose potency or have perverse effects,” Sims explained.

Case in point: Fed Chair Paul Volcker appeared to have conquered inflation when his rate hikes got CPI to fall from 14% in 1980 to 3% in 1983. 

But the market was unconvinced: The yield on 30-year Treasurys in 1983 was _11%_.

Long-term interest rates remained eight percentage points above inflation because investors were sure the government’s annual deficit of $200 billion would cause inflation to come roaring back — another rake handle to the face.

Capturing the mood, economist Ed Yardeni coined the term “Bond Vigilantes” that same year. “If the fiscal and monetary authorities won't regulate the economy,” he wrote, “the bond investors will.”

By keeping Treasury yields so far above inflation, the bond market was effectively demanding that the US government get its fiscal house in order.

It worked.

To bring interest rates down, Ronald Reagan raised taxes, cut spending, and raised the retirement age for Social Security. George Bush signed a law — PAYGO — dictating that any new entitlement spending or tax cuts had to be fully offset by spending cuts or tax increases elsewhere. Bill Clinton raised taxes on Social Security and cut spending on Medicare.

As a result, the US government ran an annual surplus in 1999, its first since 1969. 

The fiscal discipline was expected to continue.

Happy Tuesday! *Bitcoin's* surge is being fueled by improving liquidity, renewed ETF demand, and short covering, with *LMAX Group* market strategist *Joel Kruger* telling The Block the rebound is gradually strengthening the cryptocurrency's credibility among traditional investors.

In today's newsletter, *bitcoin* briefly tops $80,000, a *Las Vegas* businessman faces 280 years in prison for crypto fraud, *Franklin Templeton* partners with *HashKey* to offer a tokenized money market fund, and more.

Meanwhile, *Robinhood Chain* DEX *Arcus* launched ( https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-08-25-robinhood-chain-dex-arcus-ptokens-perps-erc-20s-412696?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) pTokens to turn perp accounts into transferable *ERC-20s*.

*P.S.* Don't forget to check out today's reader poll on *U.S. PCE* later in the newsletter.

*THE BIG ONE*

*📈 Bitcoin briefly tops $80,000; bull market case 'early but optimistic,' analyst says*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-08-25-bitcoin-holds-above-80000-412674?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Bitcoin* briefly touched a multi-month high of $81,000 on Tuesday before easing back below $80,000, extending last week's rally and pushing the Crypto Fear & Greed Index to "Extreme Greed" at 83.

* *Presto* Associate Researcher *Min Jung* said the move was a "catch-up trade" rather than a new bull cycle, as bitcoin has lagged other risk assets for some time.
* *BTSE* COO *Jeff Mei* was also cautious, saying he'd need to see bitcoin hold $100,000 for a month and the *Federal Reserve* signal rate cuts before presuming a bull market.
* However, others see a shift in trend, with *Arctic Digital* Head of Research *Justin d'Anethan* highlighting bitcoin's record weekly U.S. dollar candle and the *Treasury's* rate-easing buyback plans, saying it's "early, but one can't help but feel optimistic."
* Meanwhile, *Zeus Research* analyst *Dominick John* said this week's *PCE* inflation data is the next key test, as Presto's Jung warned that 30-year Treasury yields at their highest since 2007 still point to a tougher macro backdrop.
